parts.label: (a)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Use the correct chain rule (and quotient rule if used), including the factor $-3\cos^2\theta$ from differentiating $\cos^3\theta$, to obtain a form equivalent to $(-3\cos^2\theta)(-\sin\theta)/\cos^6\theta$. [M1] Obtain the given form $3\sin\theta\sec^4\theta$ from full correct working with signs shown; condone only the printed derivative-notation variants. [A1 AG] Total: 2.

parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Separate variables correctly, e.g. $\int \sin\theta/\cos^4\theta\,d\theta=\int (x+3)/(x^2+9)\,dx$; condone missing integral signs or one differential, but not both. [B1] Obtain a term of the form $p\sec^3\theta+A$, with $p\ne0$. [B1] Use a valid method on the $x$ integral, splitting $x/(x^2+9)+3/(x^2+9)$ or substituting $x=3\tan\phi$, to obtain one logarithmic and one inverse-tangent term. [*M1] Obtain both $q\ln(x^2+9)$ and $r\tan^{-1}(x/3)$ terms. [DM1] Obtain $\sec^3\theta=\frac32\ln(x^2+9)+3\tan^{-1}(x/3)+C$, or exact equivalent with the two different variables. [A1] Use $x=3,\theta=\pi/3$ in an equation containing all three required term types to evaluate the constant (or use correct definite limits). [M1] Obtain $C=8-\frac{3\pi}{4}-\frac32\ln18$, or exact equivalent / $1.308\ldots$. [A1] Obtain $\cos\theta=0.601$ (AWRT). [A1] Total: 8.
